newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tung aide says HK property speculation rampant.
newsitem.headline: Tung aide says HK property speculation rampant.

text.p: A senior aide to Hong Kong's future leader said property speculation was rampant in the territory and should be brought under control, local media reported on Saturday.

C.Y. Leung, a member of future Hong Kong Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa's Executive Council, said he had completed a report outlining ideas to curb property speculation in the territory, TVB News reported.

"The state of mind of speculators is much worse now," Leung told reporters. "In the past they would at least keep the flats for a while, but right now some speculators don't even look at the property (before reselling it)."

Leung, a property surveyor who was named by Tung as head of a post-colonial committee to map out long-term housing strategy, gave no details on his proposals but said they would not affect long-term investors or genuine home buyers, TVB reported.

ATV News quoted Leung as saying the imminent handover of the British colony to China on July 1 was no reason to hold off taking action on rising property prices, which are seen as a barometer of confidence in Hong Kong's future prospects.
"We should not let speculative activities spin out of control simply because we are close to the reunification or setting up the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region," he told reporters.
Leung said speculation was spreading from the luxury segment of the market, where prices had shot up early in the year, toward the middle segment, ATV reported.
